newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to help troubled property sector - bankers.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to help troubled property sector - bankers.

text.p: Olarn Chaipravat, head of the Thai Bankers Association, said on Wednesday that the government had agreed to set up an institution to offer loans to Thai property companies struggling to secure funds.

"We have agreed to set up a special financial institution to help the battered property sector," said Olarn after a meeting on the issue between bankers, the Association of Finance Companies and the Bank of Thailand. However, he did not elaborate on when the plan would take effect.
Likening the new entity to the Government Housing Bank, Olarn said it would be owned by the government and issue bonds to raise funds.
These funds would then be offered as loans to property firms having difficulty securing funds.
Thailand's property market and stocks have been hit hard by prolonged high domestic interest rates, which have slowed sales growth and increased company funding costs.
Rumours have abounded in past weeks that some property firms may be facing cash flow problems and might default on loans from financial institutions.
The news, in addition to foreign bargain-hunting, gave property and finance company stocks a lift on the local bourse. Both sectors had been heavily sold recently.

Finance firms are said by analysts to have extended an average of around 24 percent of their loan portfolios into the property sector leading to concerns about systemic risks should a large property company fold.
Among stocks rising the maximum 10 percent ceiling for the day were property firms Juldis Development Plc, Rattana Real Estate Plc and National Finance and Securities.
